root_cause.text: The intel_pstate turbo-disable path iterated over all possible CPUs and dereferenced `all_cpu_data[cpu]` even for offline CPUs with no cpufreq policy, so `store_no_turbo` could hit a NULL pointer when `no_turbo` was written on systems booted with `nosmt` or `maxcpus`.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE says `for_each_possible_cpu()` “returns CPUs even if they are not online,” and for those CPUs `all_cpu_data[] will be NULL`; after commit `973207ae3d7c`, `all_cpu_data[] is dereferenced even for CPUs which are not online, causing the NULL pointer dereference`. The patch fixes this by changing `intel_pstate_update_max_freq()` to take a CPU number, calling `cpufreq_cpu_get(cpu)`, and only using `all_cpu_data[cpu]` for CPUs with a valid cpufreq policy.

intent_record.intent_summary: Refactor max-frequency update handling to use a CPU ID and look up the associated per-CPU data internally.
intent_record.what: The function `intel_pstate_update_max_freq` was changed to take an `int cpu` argument instead of a `struct cpudata *cpudata`, and it now calls `cpufreq_cpu_get(cpu)` and passes `all_cpu_data[cpu]` to `__intel_pstate_update_max_freq()` instead of using `cpudata->cpu` and the original `cpudata` pointer.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the helper now resolves the per-CPU policy and cpudata from a CPU number rather than relying on a cpudata object being passed in. This changes the call contract and makes the update path operate from a CPU identifier, while still performing the same max-frequency refresh when a policy exists.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix the max-frequency update loop to pass the CPU identifier instead of per-CPU data.
intent_record.what: In the loop over all possible CPUs, the call to `intel_pstate_update_max_freq()` was changed from passing `all_cpu_data[cpu]` to passing `cpu` directly.
intent_record.how: This changes the argument type/value supplied to `intel_pstate_update_max_freq()`, so the function now receives the CPU index rather than the per-CPU data pointer/object. At runtime, this affects which CPU context the max-frequency update operates on and likely corrects the call to match the function's expected parameter.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix the max-frequency update work handler to pass the CPU ID to `intel_pstate_update_max_freq()`.
intent_record.what: In `intel_pstate_notify_work()`, the argument passed to `intel_pstate_update_max_freq()` was changed from `cpudata` to `cpudata->cpu`.
intent_record.how: This changes the call site to pass the CPU identifier instead of the `cpudata` structure, matching the expected function interface and allowing the max frequency update path to operate on the correct CPU context.

relevance_review.reason: The change is a refactor of max-frequency update handling, using a CPU ID to find per-CPU data internally. It does not address the turbo-disable path or the NULL dereference from iterating over offline CPUs in store_no_turbo.

The changes fix a max-frequency update work handler by passing the CPU ID correctly, but the root cause is a NULL dereference in the turbo-disable (`store_no_turbo`) path when iterating over offline CPUs without cpufreq policy. This group does not address that code path or the offline-CPU NULL pointer issue.

candidates.rationale: This loop iterates over every possible CPU and unconditionally dereferences all_cpu_data[cpu]. For offline CPUs with no cpufreq policy, that entry can be NULL, which matches the NULL pointer crash described in the root cause.

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement dereferences all_cpu_data[cpu] while iterating over all possible CPUs. On offline CPUs without a cpufreq policy, all_cpu_data[cpu] can be NULL, so the turbo-disable path can crash with a NULL pointer as described.

    cpufreq: intel_pstate: Rearrange max frequency updates handling code
    
    Rename __intel_pstate_update_max_freq() to intel_pstate_update_max_freq()

    implement the locking with the recently introduced cpufreq policy "write"

bic_trace_step.reason: The vulnerable construct described in the root cause was a turbo-disable path that iterated over all possible CPUs and dereferenced `all_cpu_data[cpu]` even for offline CPUs with no cpufreq policy. In this snippet, the relevant loops no longer do that unsafe policy dereference pattern: `intel_pstate_update_limits_for_all()` now does `for_each_possible_cpu(cpu) intel_pstate_update_max_freq(all_cpu_data[cpu]);`, and the updated helper immediately checks `policy = cpufreq_cpu_get(cpudata->cpu); if (!policy) return false;` before accessing policy-dependent state. Likewise, `intel_pstate_update_limits()` now calls `if (intel_pstate_update_max_freq(cpudata)) hybrid_update_capacity(cpudata);` instead of assuming a valid policy exists. This shows the fix is already present: offline CPUs without a policy are skipped by the early `if (!policy) return false;` guard, preventing the NULL dereference. Therefore the vulnerable construct is not present in this commit version.
